newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 4.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--Trading on the Athens Stock Exchange yesterday saw buyers switch their interest from banking to construction shares, forced the general price index down by 1.55 percent to close at 1,148.06 points. Sources say the corrective movement in banking prices was expected and gives the market the breathing space to place new capital.

--Keeping a lid on wage increases and strictly following the declared incomes policy will be an issue of major importance for the government over the next few months. National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou has asked state-run banks to follow an incomes policy that will not see their wage bill exceed 7.0 percent, meaning increases of 4.0-5.0 percent for bank staff.

--The Interamerican Group has expressed interest in participating in the General Bank. This would take the form either of participation in the imminent share capital increase or by a share package transfer, according to sources from the Group.

--A new subsidiary - the International National Bank of Greece - will be included in the National Bank's portfolio as part of its efforts to expand activity around the globe. The International National will be based in the U.K. and spearhead the bank's investment activity abroad.
IMERISIA

--The noose strikers have thrown around the neck of the economy is tightening, with bank employees indicating they may hit the streets along with teachers and public servants. The wave of industrial action does not appear to be abating and is beginning to constitute a serious threat to the healthy course of the economy.
--The merger of subsidiaries belonging to Commercial and Ionian Banks is the first step towards the eventual merger of the two banks, reports say.
--The Agricultural Bank of Greece is slowly extricating itself from 30 subsidiaries, part of its expansion programme which will see the bank receive 25 billion drachmas per annum.
KERDOS
--Yesterday's eventful auction of 12-month Treasury bills finally brought the state 390 billion drachmas.

--Major public works projects - such as the Egnatia Highway, the Athens Metro and the National Land Register - have noted significant delays in the absorption of European Union funds and in the course of work. A meeting at the national economy ministry examined ways to overcome obstacles.
--The two major share holders in men's and women's ready-to-wear Artisti Italiani look likely to take their dispute to the courts.
EXPRESS

--Thessaly farmers hope to make good on their threats of a second go at disrupting national road and rail links today, following a late night decision to set up blockades at five points on the national roads. Both government and farmers, however, appear determined to have their final showdown. "We never set or accept ultimatums," a government spokesman said.
--The implementation of the TAXIS computerised taxation system within 1998 will mean the end of the controversial "objective tax criteria".
--Tax revenues were at satisfactory levels for the months of January with sources saying that the budget forecast of an average increase of 14.6 percent is attainable.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Warburg Credit Swiss is to submit proposals on the future of the Ionian Bank soon. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
